title: A ring map is perfect exactly when the target has a finite resolution by finite projectives over a polynomial algebra
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises a perfect ring map A -> B by the existence of a presentation B = A[x_1, ..., x_n]/I together with a finite resolution of B by finite projective A[x_1, ..., x_n]-modules (source lines 21773-21778). The proof runs the two implications. For a perfect A -> B, the proof uses that B is pseudo-coherent as an A[x_1, ..., x_n]-module and has finite tor dimension as an A-module; the perfect-over-a-polynomial-ring lemma then makes B perfect as an A[x_1, ..., x_n]-module, which by the perfect-module statement means it has a finite resolution by finite projective A[x_1, ..., x_n]-modules (proof lines 21781-21787). Conversely, given such a resolution, B is pseudo-coherent as an A[x_1, ..., x_n]-module, hence A -> B is pseudo-coherent; and the given resolution over A[x_1, ..., x_n] is in particular a finite resolution by flat A-modules, so B has finite tor dimension as an A-module (proof lines 21788-21794). The two conditions together are exactly the definition of a perfect ring map, which closes the equivalence. The non-routine content is the pairing of relative pseudo-coherence with finite tor dimension over the base in each direction.
